primary_meaning: Jesus Christ (the divine Logos/Son), as the personal embodiment and personification of God's wisdom
primary_basis: Proverbs 8:22-31 (Wisdom present/begotten before creation and active in it)
1 Corinthians 1:24 ('Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God')
Colossians 2:3 (all treasures of wisdom hidden in Christ)
Matthew 11:19 / Luke 7:35 (wisdom justified by her deeds/children, applied to Jesus)

alternatives.meaning: Literary/poetic personification of a divine attribute (God's wise ordering of creation and moral call) without hypostatic or christological identification

basis: occasional patristic associations of Sophia with the Spirit
certain pneumatological readings of Wisdom literature

alternatives.meaning: A semi-divine feminine figure or archetype (Sophia)
basis: some modern feminist or sophiological theologies

notes: Traditional Christian exegesis (patristic through confessional) overwhelmingly reads personified Wisdom christologically as a type or hypostasis of the Son; modern biblical studies commonly prefers a non-ontological literary reading while still acknowledging the later christological application. The christological sense remains the dominant symbolic assignment in Christian teaching.
